title: RSI — the 7 P's, Drugs & Post-Intubation
sources: Critical Vector — EM Pocket Guide: RSI 7 P's + Post-Intubation Management
ACEP airway guidance (2023); standard emergency airway management (Walls / Manual of Emergency Airway Management)

changelog.change: Initial entry — the 7 P's, induction-agent and NMB selection tables with doses, LEMON, CICO, and the post-intubation settings + hypotension checklist.

summary: Preparation · Preoxygenation · Pretreatment (optional) · Paralysis & induction · Positioning · Placement with confirmation · Post-intubation care. Push the induction agent and paralytic together (no fasciculation wait). Confirm with waveform capnography every time. For the physiologically fragile patient, see the physiologically-difficult-airway reference first.

items: 1. Preparation — monitoring, suction, BVM, laryngoscope + blade, ETT (7.5 F / 8.0 M) + stylet, EtCO2 detector, and a surgical airway kit at the bedside. Assign roles.

2. Preoxygenation — NRB 15 L/min for 3 min, or HFNC 60 L/min, or CPAP/NIV 5 cmH2O; target SpO2 ≥ 96–99% before the attempt. Keep apnoeic oxygenation (nasal cannula 15 L/min) running through the attempt. Use NIV/BVM-with-PEEP, not a nonrebreather alone, if the SpO2 won't climb (PREOXI).
3. Pretreatment (optional) — fentanyl 3 mcg/kg to blunt the sympathetic response (aortic dissection, raised ICP, ACS); lidocaine 1.5 mg/kg is of marginal benefit and often omitted.
4. Paralysis & induction — give the induction agent and the NMB together (no wait for fasciculations).
5. Positioning — ear-to-sternal-notch; ramp the obese patient; sniffing position; head of bed up.
6. Placement with proof — direct or video laryngoscopy, tube through the cords, inflate the cuff, CONFIRM with waveform capnography (a sustained tracing over ≥ 6 breaths).

Neutral to ↑ BP (indirect sympathomimetic; direct depressant unmasked in catecholamine-depleted shock)
Shock, asthma, bronchospasm. Avoid uncontrolled hypertension / aortic dissection. RSI trial (2025): no safer than etomidate, more collapse — dose-reduce + pressor-ready
The most haemodynamically stable single agent. Single dose only — transient adrenal suppression (debated clinical significance in septic shock)
1.5–2 mg/kg IV (halve in the elderly / ASA III–IV)
Status epilepticus, raised ICP, elective airways. Avoid in hypotension / haemodynamic fragility
Variable depth, slower onset — rarely first choice for RSI
Fastest; short duration. CONTRAINDICATED: burns / crush / denervation > 48–72 h old, pre-existing hyperkalaemia, myopathy, prior malignant hyperthermia, pseudocholinesterase deficiency
Preferred when succinylcholine is contraindicated. Duration ~45–70 min — fully reversible with sugammadex 16 mg/kg for immediate rescue

items: Look externally — obesity, beard, small mouth, facial trauma, large tongue.
Evaluate 3-3-2 — mouth opening ≥ 3 fingers, hyoid-to-chin ≥ 3 fingers, thyroid-to-mouth-floor ≥ 2 fingers.
Obstruction / Obesity — stridor, abscess, epiglottitis, neck mass.
Neck mobility reduced — c-collar, arthritis, halo.

body.text: CICO (cannot intubate, cannot oxygenate): declare it out loud and go to a surgical airway IMMEDIATELY — scalpel–finger–bougie–tube. Do NOT keep re-attempting laryngoscopy.

rows: 6–8 mL/kg ideal body weight (6 if ARDS or at risk)
12–16/min — adjust to match the pre-intubation minute ventilation and keep pH ≥ 7.35
5 cmH2O (raise per the ARDSNet ladder if ARDS)
1:2 (1:3–4 for asthma / COPD to avoid air trapping)

items: Confirm: waveform capnography (flat = oesophageal or arrest), bilateral breath sounds + no epigastric sounds, CXR with the tube tip 3–5 cm above the carina. Secure the tube; document the cm mark at the lips.
Sedation + analgesia: propofol 5–50 mcg/kg/min OR dexmedetomidine 0.2–1.5 mcg/kg/hr, plus a fentanyl infusion. Analgesia first, then titrate sedation to a light target (RASS 0 to −1).

Post-intubation hypotension — reduce the PEEP, exclude a tension pneumothorax, treat hypovolaemia (give fluid / push-dose pressor), and check for a right-main-bronchus intubation (pull the tube back).
